summary: Adaptive autoscale lag causing transient kernel OOMs and degraded throughput for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
BrightHealth's dedicated pool observed a sustained throughput degradation over a 3-hour window. Autoscaler lagged behind a sudden spike in request concurrency from one tenant, causing multiple containers to be co-located on the same GPU and triggering kernel-level OOM errors in the serving runtime. Impact: customer reports 35-60% higher p95 latency and a subset of requests failing with transient 5xx errors.

Impact:
- Production traffic for BrightHealth (dedicated tier) saw increased p95 from ~350ms to ~1.2s for generation requests.
- ~7% of requests returned 5xx (internal server error) tied to runtime kernel OOMs.
- Customer-facing features degraded for ~3 hours; they reported partial rollback to earlier model variant as workaround.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id dp-7643 (BrightHealth); autoscale policy: adaptive-v2 (scale-up threshold CPU/gpu saturation + queue depth).
- Region: us-east-1, GPU type: A100-40GB (mixture of 80GB earlier VMs but this pool is 40GB).
- Serving runtime: 2026-02-28 build, kernel: cuda-12.3 + custom memory manager.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1. Generate synthetic burst pattern matching customer's traffic: 120 concurrent streams with varying sequence lengths (avg 512 tokens) for ~5m.
2. Observe autoscaler decision lag and node provisioning times.
3. Monitor GPU allocations and kernel logs for OOM / NVML warnings.

Logs & quick evidence:
- Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dp-7643/throughput/2026-03-12
- Kernel OOM traces (summarized): repeated "cuMemAlloc failed" and serving-runtime tracebacks referencing KV cache allocation at high sequence lengths.
- Scheduler events show scale-up triggers at T+40s but worker readiness only at T+210s (provisioning latency).
- Observability: sudden per-GPU process count increases, indicating co-located containers prior to scale-up.

Customer notes:
- Customer attempted short-term mitigation by pinning to a smaller model and saw latency reduce but still observed occasional 5xx.
- Customer requests permanent mitigation and guidance to avoid recurrence.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage completed. Customer impact confirmed. Escalated to SRE. Assigned to Diego.

2026-03-12 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Collecting GPU-level logs and autoscaler events. Reproduced provisioning lag in staging with synthetic load. Suspect provisioning latency + oversubscription as root cause.

2026-03-13 - Priya Nair (Scheduler Eng): Observed that adaptive-v2 policy uses spot-backed nodes which occasionally return slower readiness time during current region capacity pressure. Opening hypothesis: spot preemption + delayed instance boot causing temporary GPU shortages.

2026-03-13 - BrightHealth Technical Lead (customer): Provided traffic traces and confirmed burst window originates from nightly batch plus manual testing. Asked about recommended autoscale configuration for bursty traffic.

2026-03-14 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Applied mitigation in prod: increased min-reserved nodes for BrightHealth pool to reduce autoscale dependency during burst. Monitoring shows p95 latency returning toward baseline. Will keep ticket open for follow-up actions.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Autoscaler decision latency + slow instance boot/attach leads to temporary GPU shortage and packing of containers onto fewer GPUs, causing memory pressure and kernel OOMs.

Hypothesis B: Noisy tenant behavior (bursting to high concurrency) exceeds previously profiled sequence length distribution; KV cache allocations larger than typical leading to per-request memory spike.

Telemetry findings: Node provisioning median cold-start = 190s in us-east-1 over past 24h (outlier 350s). Scheduler logs show back-to-back placement attempts that co-locate pods when recently requested capacity not yet ready.

Serving-runtime: memory accounting does not pre-reserve KV cache headroom for high-seq requests; when multiple high-seq requests land on same GPU, aggregated allocations exceed available and trigger cuMemAlloc failure.

Reproduction: In staging, running 100 concurrent streams with avg 512 tokens reproduced kernel OOM within 3-6 minutes when min-reserved nodes = 0. With min-reserved nodes = 2, no OOMs observed during identical load.
Related: See SUP-30877 for a prior noisy-tenant allocation pattern; not identical but similar symptoms. Linked INT-924 where scheduler team is experimenting with soft preemption heuristics.
resolution:
Mitigation applied 2026-03-14: increased min-reserved capacity for dp-7643 and tuned autoscaler thresholds to favor faster scale-up for queue-depth signals. Customer advised to reduce simultaneous long-seq bursts as short-term operational change.

Follow-ups (post-mitigation):
- Scheduler: implement soft preemption to pre-empt low-priority co-located containers when GPU memory pressure detected (INT-924).
- Serving-runtime: add conservative KV cache headroom accounting and a high-seq circuit breaker to avoid cuMemAlloc cascades. PR referenced above.
- SRE/Capacity: review instance types used for dedicated pools and avoid spot-backed instance types for high-SLO customers, or provide explicit guidance/documentation for burst windows.

Status: Customer impacted window mitigated; monitoring shows p95 latency trending back to baseline. Ticket remains open pending code changes and capacity plan (ETA for fixes: 3 weeks).
